jobs.title: Community Development Director
jobs.description:
Job Description

An opportunity to help shape the future of one of Northern California's most iconic small towns in a moment of exciting economic development and sustainable growth!

The City of Healdsburg is conducting an important search for an experienced professional to serve as their next Community Development Director. The ideal candidate will be a dedicated and focused leader who can balance the City's rich history and culture with a forward-thinking commitment to ensure long-term success and stability. They will be a collaborative and solution-oriented member of the City's executive team.

The Community Development Director plans, organizes, directs and reviews the activities of the Community Development Department including the administration and operation of planning, land use, development standards, building safety, and protection of the City's natural and cultural resources. The ideal candidate will have a customer-friendly approach to plan review and permitting, seeking solutions and efficiency while maintaining adherence to codes and regulations. This is an exciting opportunity to oversee a high volume of complex development activity, including affordable housing, hotels, and mixed-use projects.

The City of Healdsburg is idyllically situated amongst three picturesque valleys in the heart of Sonoma County's wine country. Located 65 miles north of San Francisco, the City was incorporated in 1867 and seamlessly pairs a vibrant small-town atmosphere with access to the amenities and conveniences of a large metropolitan area. The City's 11,172 residents enjoy a lively and engaging downtown experience centered around the Spanish-style Healdsburg Plaza which is renowned for its shopping, dining, and art galleries. The City is rich with heritage and hosts a diverse array of community events throughout the year, cherishing its small-town character, architectural charm and history.

Qualifications For Consideration

Education:
Equivalent to a Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university with major course work in regional planning, urban planning, environmental planning, public administration, business administration, or a related field. A Master's degree is preferred.

Experience:
Seven years of increasingly responsible experience in professional urban or regional planning; including three years of administrative and management responsibility.

Compensation And Benefits

The current annual salary range for the Community Development Director position is $186,549.12 to $226,755.36. Placement within this range is negotiable and dependent upon experience and qualifications. The City of Healdsburg offers an attractive benefits package, including CalPERS retirement.

Application and Selection Process

Interested candidates should apply by submitting a compelling cover letter and comprehensive resume via email to apply@ralphandersen.com no later than Monday, November 2, 2026
. This is a confidential recruitment and will be handled accordingly throughout the various stages of the process. Confidential inquiries are welcomed and should be directed to Sabrina Landreth, Ralph Andersen & Associates, at sabrina@ralphandersen.com or (916) 630-4900.

For more information, please visit the posting on our website at https://ralphandersen.com/jobs/community-development-director-healdsburg-ca/

jobs.title: Chief Development Officer
jobs.description:
FULL TIME JOB VACANCY

CHIEF DEVELOPMENT OFFICER

Development and Outreach Department

Multiple Locations Considered (NYC Preferred)

Application Deadline: Open Until Filled

The Role

The Chief Development Officer (CDO) will bring fresh vision and strategic leadership to build on and boldly advance the organization's fundraising, marketing, and donor and community engagement efforts, deepening impact and expanding reach at a pivotal moment for HRW. This is a critical position for the organization and an exciting opportunity to shape and accelerate the fundraising strategy and roadmap for HRW's future, developing and implementing ambitious fundraising, outreach, and constituency building strategies. The CDO must be committed to HRW's mission to take on human rights abuses around the world, communicate passionately about its work, and inspire its staff, volunteer teams, and donors.

The CDO will report directly to Executive Director Philippe Bolopion and will serve on HRW's Executive Committee, the organization’s senior leadership team. The CDO will lead a high-performing Development & Outreach Team of approximately 110 staff members, spanning leadership and principal giving, donor committees and council fundraising, Board of Directors engagement, foundation giving, marketing, planned giving, and fundraising systems and data analysis.

Fundraising Context

HRW’s fundraising has grown steadily over the years, and it currently raises approximately $100M annually, with approximately 70% of its revenue from gifts of $100,000+. A focus of fundraising and outreach at HRW has been the HRW Council, a collective of some 20 committees and 1,000 individuals around the world who help fundraise, engage new constituents and potential donors, partner with local organizations to promote human rights issues, and advocate on behalf of HRW and its mission. The CDO will be responsible for growing existing revenue streams and diversifying the organization’s income through principal, leadership and major gifts, institutional funding, marketing, and planned giving to ensure the long-term health and sustainability of the organization.

The greatest opportunity for the CDO lies in engaging donors at the highest levels to support major strategic work while also determining the optimal level of resources for growing the base of support. In 2024, HRW adopted a five-year Global Strategy to guide the organization’s programmatic and operational direction. In July 2026, the strategy was refined to help position HRW for maximum impact in a rapidly shifting human rights environment. The CDO will shape how HRW grows and diversifies revenue to support the organization’s strategic priorities and deliver on the ambitions set out in the refined strategy.

Underpinning all of this is a mandate for stability and steady leadership. HRW seeks a CDO who will lead the function credibly over the long term – reinforcing continuity, strengthening the pipeline, and building the confidence of the Development & Outreach Team. The CDO will partner closely with an engaged Board, providing the structure and clear, well-framed strategies that enable board members to fundraise effectively, and bringing the judgment and gravitas to offer candid counsel to both the Board and the Executive Director. The Executive Director is a highly effective, door-opening presence with donors, and the CDO will amplify that strength through strategic partnership, disciplined preparation, and timely briefings. Finally, the CDO will invest in the Development & Outreach Team itself – building capacity, fostering trust across a distributed group, and marrying HRW's activist passion with professional fundraising rigor.

Key Responsibilities

Play a critical leadership role in shaping the organization's overall strategy and multi-year financial planning, working closely with the Executive Committee and Finance team to align revenue growth with organizational priorities;
Translate those priorities into an ambitious multi-year development and fundraising strategy, developing and implementing compelling plans and campaigns that inspire donors and partners to join HRW in addressing unprecedented challenges to human rights;
Provide strategic direction across all aspects of HRW fundraising and outreach activities, including leadership gifts, foundations, marketing, donor experiences, planned giving, development operations and analysis, donor committees and board engagement;
Represent HRW’s work to donors, prospects, and the Council to cultivate and grow the organization’s base of support;
Set and meet fundraising objectives, monitor and evaluate progress, and pivot strategy as needed to capitalize on emerging opportunities and maximize impact;
Develop comprehensive, ambitious funding proposals that will engage and inspire top-tier donors to make transformational gifts;
Champion diversity, equity, and inclusion within the Development & Outreach Team and across relationships with donors, board, and committee members;
Determine the appropriate short and long-term investments in development, setting budgets, leveraging data analytics, and maximizing revenue while building a robust pipeline of major and planned giving donors;
Collaborate across the organization to ensure development activities are well coordinated with and supportive of organizational priorities;
Support and amplify fundraising efforts of the Executive Director, senior leadership, and Development & Outreach Team;
Sustain and strengthen Board of Directors engagement and stewardship in consultation with organizational leadership;
Lead, motivate and mentor a high performing team, setting clear expectations, establishing performance objectives, providing timely and constructive feedback, supporting professional growth, and attending to staff well- being and resilience;
Foster an inclusive, positive work environment where all staff feel welcome, heard and able to succeed, actively soliciting diverse perspectives, advancing equity and inclusion, and addressing any bias or discrimination proactively; and
Perform other tasks as may be required.

Candidate Profile

The Chief Development Officer will be a collaborative, innovative, and visionary leader with exceptional people, communications, and management skills and the passion and capacity to lead a sophisticated global fundraising operation. They will bring high intellectual and emotional intelligence, sharp cultural awareness, and the ability to communicate and influence effectively across a complex, highly distributed organization. The ideal candidate will understand the nuances of fundraising across multiple geographies and cultures, inspire and motivate experienced teams, and embody a deep commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion. They will be passionate about HRW's mission and able to articulate a compelling vision that engages staff, volunteers, advocates, and donors, and catalyzes giving.

Ideal Experience

At least 12 to 15 years of fundraising experience, with at least five (5) years of experience in a senior role such as Chief Development Officer, Deputy Chief Development Officer, or equivalent.
A deep commitment to HRW's mission of defending the rights of people worldwide, and the ability to communicate about its work with passion and conviction.
Proven experience leading and motivating fundraising teams in a complex, global organization, setting ambitious objectives, managing performance, and driving results.
Expertise across major gift fundraising, marketing, capital campaigns, and planned giving, with a keen awareness of evolving trends and best practices.
A strong track record of cultivating and closing transformational gifts from major donors, including foundations.
The ability to master, represent, and compellingly communicate the organization's mission and programs to diverse audiences.
A global perspective on philanthropy and the cultural competency to work effectively with staff, donors, and board and committee members across geographies.
An ability to foster an inclusive team culture characterized by creativity, collegiality, mutual respect, and professional growth.
Outstanding oral and written communications skills in English; proficiency in additional languages is a plus.
A data-driven approach to developing, implementing, and measuring fundraising strategies, with a demonstrated ability to drive transformational growth.
Superior analytical, strategic planning, and problem-solving skills.

LOCATION AND COMPENSATION

This position is preferably based in HRW's New York office, with other HRW offices a possibility, and requires a flexible schedule to accommodate colleagues across multiple time zones. The role involves both domestic and international travel, approximately 25–40% of the time.

The estimated compensation for this position if based in the United States is $350,000 – 400,000. Compensation ranges in other locations vary according to the local market. Additionally, HRW offers comprehensive Total Rewards package. Relocation assistance and immigration support are available if required, and people of all nationalities are encouraged to apply.

Job Description

Join Employee Platforms as an Executive Director, Portfolio & Execution within the central Engineering & Architecture (E&A) function. This role reports solid line to the Head of Engineering & Architecture (E&A) and serves as the primary leader for portfolio governance, execution transparency, and operating cadence across E&A.

You will partner with the Head of E&A and E&A senior leaders, including the Head of Engineering, the Head of Architecture, E&A domain leaders (core engineering, data architecture, AI architecture, architecture governance), and dotted-line Chief Architects across Employee Platforms towers. You will help these leaders organize strategy into coherent programs and then drive and monitor their books of work through disciplined planning, metrics, governance, and executive-ready reporting.

Job Responsibilities

Own the integrated E&A portfolio, translating strategy into roadmaps, annual priorities, quarterly OKRs, milestones, dependencies, benefits, and risks.
Run the E&A operating cadence, including portfolio and delivery health reviews, dependency and risk management, escalations, and decision governance.
Produce executive-ready reporting on progress, outcomes, risks, and decisions, maintaining a single source of truth across E&A.

Strong executive communication skills, including concise written materials and the ability to synthesize complex initiatives into clear plans and decision-ready options.

Basic AI skills (working fluency): AI evaluation literacy, effective collaboration with technical SMEs, practical prompting for drafting/synthesis/analysis, and responsible AI awareness to support safe adoption in partnership with control and risk stakeholders.

jobs.title: Managing Director, Data, AI and Applied Technology
jobs.description:
What We Can Achieve Together

The Managing Director, Data, AI & Applied Technology advances The Nature Conservancy (TNC)'s conservation mission by defining how data, applied technology, and artificial intelligence create measurable mission and business value. This is a newly created role and a first-of-its-kind function at TNC: it owns the “what, who, and why” of data, applied technology, and AI, including what decisions must improve, what outcomes matter most, where data can create mission advantage, and how emerging technologies should be responsibly explored and applied. The role then translates these insights into coordinated, collaborative execution to deliver measurable outcomes.

This role leads enterprise business data strategy, domain data ownership, data governance accountability, responsible AI governance, use-case prioritization, value realization, and adoption, and partners closely with the CIO organization, which owns technical data platforms, architecture, engineering, controls, and scalable delivery.

Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer with a dotted line to the Chief Executive Officer, and a dotted-line partnership with the Chief Information Officer, the Managing Director serves as TNC's senior authority on business data and AI strategy and governance, applied and emerging conservation technology, the NatureChat and conservation intelligence workstreams, technology partnerships, and external thought leadership and cross-NGO positioning.

In This Role, You Will

Develop and maintain TNC's enterprise business data, applied technology, and AI strategies, aligned to conservation priorities and organizational goals.
Establish and mature a federated domain data ownership model across Conservation, Science, Development/Membership, Marketing, HR, Finance, Legal, Operations, and other enterprise domains.
Lead enterprise data governance from a business accountability perspective, and establish responsible AI governance guidance, acceptable-use expectations, and risk-review processes.
Build executive and domain-leader commitment to data stewardship, data quality, responsible AI, and adoption, and develop data and AI literacy programs in partnership with People, Learning, IT, and business domains.
Build and manage a high-performing, globally aware team spanning business data strategy and governance, responsible AI, portfolio management, adoption, and data culture.
Operate as an enterprise partner and trusted advisor to the Executive Leadership Team, and represent TNC in external forums on responsible AI, conservation data, and mission-driven data strategy.
Manage an annual operating budget covering team, tools, and external services, and negotiate and manage contracts with vendors and service partners.

You will navigate the unique dynamics of a globally federated organization, building consensus across regions and business units while maintaining enterprise standards, and champion a culture where people at every level can confidently use data to make decisions.

We’re Looking For You

Are you energized by the chance to build something that has never existed at TNC before? This is a rare opportunity to shape a brand-new enterprise function from the ground up, one that will define how data, applied technology, and artificial intelligence help protect the lands and waters all life depends on.

You will work at the center of TNC's federated, global structure, partnering with the Chief Operating Officer, Chief Executive Officer, Chief Information Officer, and Executive Leadership Team to translate emerging technology into real conservation and business outcomes. You will help TNC evolve into an organization where timely, trusted data informs decisions at every level, from field-based conservation teams to the executive suite.

If you thrive on ambiguity, enjoy building consensus across a complex global organization, and want your work on data and AI to translate directly into mission impact, we would love to hear from you. This position is hybrid, with a preference for candidates based in the Washington, DC metro area near TNC's Arlington, VA office, though flexibility exists for candidates located elsewhere.

What You’ll Bring

Bachelor's degree in business, law, data science, data governance, natural resource management, or other relevant field and 10 or more years of experience, including 5 years of experience at a senior level in a global and/or multi-product line organization, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
Experience in partnership development with corporations, community leaders, governments, and non-profit organizations in multiple countries, including experience with high-level government and conservation contacts.
Experience translating organizational strategy into data, analytics, applied technology, or AI-enabled business outcomes.
Experience with executive-level communication and influence, including building credibility with non-technical senior audiences and technical partners.
Experience leading governance, decision rights, adoption strategies, change management, and benefits realization across a matrixed organization.
Experience with data privacy, security, ethical data use, responsible AI, and inclusive change leadership.

Desired Qualifications

Graduate degree in business, law, data science, data governance, natural resource management, and/or other relevant field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
Experience in global, federated, or mission-driven organizations.
Experience establishing federated data governance, responsible AI governance, domain data ownership, or data product operating models.
Familiarity with conservation science data, geospatial data, fundraising or donor data, marketing data, HR or people data, finance data, or comparable complex data domains.
Track record building organizational data literacy and adoption, encompassing culture and behavior change, not just tools.
Experience cultivating external technology partnerships, academic collaborations, in-kind support, or pro bono expertise.
Comfort with ambiguity and an entrepreneurial approach, including experience shaping a new enterprise function while maintaining governance discipline.

Salary Information

This position may be based in any country where TNC has an established entity, taking into consideration legal restrictions, such as non-national ratios and immigration processing times. For U.S. based applicants only, the starting pay range for this position is generally within the range of $275,000 - $330,000 for annual base salary and is based on location, qualifications, specific skills, and experience. This range includes flexibility depending on experience and unique skill sets. This range only applies to candidates whose country of employment is the USA. For all other applicants, pay ranges will be in local currency, the pay range will be based on the local labor market, and not tied to the above pay range. Your geographic location will be confirmed during the recruitment and used to determine your actual pay range. Additionally, for all applicants, actual pay will fall within a range based on a variety of factors including, for example, the candidate’s qualifications, specific skills, and experience.

Who We Are

The Nature Conservancy’s mission is to protect the lands and waters upon which all life depends. As a science-based organization, we create innovative, on-the-ground solutions to our world’s toughest challenges so that we can create a world in which people and nature thrive. We’re rooted in our mission and guided by our values, which include respect for all people, communities, and cultures. Whether it’s career development, flexible schedules, or a rewarding mission, there’s many reasons to love life inside TNC. Want a better insight to TNC? Check out our TNC Talent playlist on YouTube to hear stories from staff or visit Glassdoor.

One goal is to cultivate an inclusive work environment so that all our colleagues around the globe feel a sense of belonging and that their unique contributions to our mission are valued. In addition to the requirements in our job postings, we recognize that people come with talent and experiences outside of a job and consider each applicant’s unique experience. Please apply – we’d love to hear from you. To quote a popular saying at TNC, “you’ll join for the mission, and stay for the people.”

What We Bring

Since 1951, TNC has been doing work you can believe in. Through grassroots action, we have grown from a small non-profit into one of the most effective and wide-reaching environmental organizations in the world. Thanks to more than 1 million members, over 400 scientists, and the dedicated efforts of our diverse staff and partners, we impact conservation around the world!

TNC offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package including health care benefits, flexible spending accounts, a 401(k) plan with an 8% employer match, parental leave, accrued paid time off, life insurance, disability coverage, employee assistance program, other life and work well-being benefits. Learn more about our Benefits and Perks here.

We’re proud to offer a flexible work environment that supports of the health and well-being of the people we employ.

Our recruiting process includes a rolling interview process to ensure we engage applicants in a timely manner. This means we may review applications in the order in which they are received. Once a strong candidate pool is identified, the role will be unposted. The timeline may vary depending on the expressed interest in the role, so we highly encourage candidates to apply as soon as possible.

Employees must submit their application by logging into Workday and applying via the Jobs Hub.

Our commitment to equal employment opportunity includes the recognition that our conservation mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people of all backgrounds, beliefs, and culture. Recruiting and mentoring staff to create an inclusive organization is a priority, and we encourage applicants from all cultures, races, colors, religions, sexes, national or regional origins, ages, disability status, sexual orientation, gender identity, military, protected veteran status or other status protected by law.

The successful applicant must meet the requirements of The Nature Conservancy's background screening process.

Summary

Organizational Location: This position is with the Department of Homeland Security; within U.S. Customs and Border Protection; in the Office of Trade in Washington, D.C. For more information about U.S. Customs and Border Protection, please visit https://www.cbp.gov/about.

Duties

As Executive Director, Operations in the Office of Trade, at U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), you will oversee the coordination of national level trade initiatives and intelligence-driven trade operations. You will oversee resources and systems to fully implement a comprehensive multi-year strategic plan to effectively target and analyze national trade issues and operational initiatives. You will oversee threat assessment and targeting units, intelligence-driven civil investigation services, and the collection and analysis of trade data to quantify the economic impact of trade disruptions. You will serve as an agency authority in formulating new trade intelligence and trade investigative policies and program objectives. You will provide management and consulting services to top executives of the agency on change management and internal business process improvements to increase the effectiveness of major operations and functions. As Executive Director, will provide guidance to senior management staff and officials at multiple levels of the agency; senior staff of other federal, state, and local government agencies; and private sector clients and vendors; on matters related to the Operations and Planning Program. You will also establish and maintain collaborative working relationships with agency or Department management officials, other Government agencies, and institutions with related interests and equities to advance the Operations and Planning Program and objectives of the agency. For an overview of the diverse responsibilities CBP carries out within the Government, visit our website at www.cbp.gov

Requiremennts

Must be a U.S. Citizen. All pre-employment processes will be conducted in English. You may be required to pass a background investigation. CBP follows the DHS Drug-Free Workplace Plan for drug testing procedures. Subject to a 1-year supervisory probationary period (unless already completed). Complete a Declaration for Federal Employment to determine your suitability for Federal employment, at the time requested by the agency. If you are a male applicant born after December 31, 1959, certify that you have registered with the Selective Service System or are exempt from having to do so. May be subject to pre-employment and random drug tests File a Confidential Financial Disclosure Report OGE-278e within 30 days of appointment and annually from then on. You may be required to obtain and maintain a security clearance prior to entrance on duty. Failure to obtain and maintain the required level of clearance may result in the withdrawal of a job offer or removal. Organizational and geographical mobility is essential in developing and managing SES leaders. Individuals selected for SES positions may be subject to reassignment across geographical, organizational, and functional lines, and may be required to sign a Reassignment Rights and Obligation Agreement. There are three key documents that contain important information about your rights and obligations. Please read and retain these documents: Noncriminal Justice Applicant's Privacy Rights, for those who undergo an FBI fingerprint-based criminal history record check for personnel vetting, which includes Rap Back, FD-258 Privacy Act Statement - FBI (this is the same statement used when your fingerprints are submitted as part of your background investigation), and SEAD-3-Reporting-U.pdf (dni.gov), (applicable to those who hold a sensitive position or have eligibility for access to classified information). If you fail to meet the conditions of employment or any other pre-employment requirements, such as missing any of the scheduled appointments, the hiring agency may rescind their tentative offer of employment. You must meet the qualification requirements of this position no later than the closing date of the job opportunity announcement.

Qualifications

Candidates should be committed to improving the efficiency of the Federal government, passionate about the ideals of our American republic, and committed to upholding the rule of law and the United States Constitution. Candidates will not be hired based on their race, sex, color, religion, or national origin. As a basic requirement, applicants must demonstrate progressively responsible leadership experience that is indicative of senior executive level managerial capability and directly related to the skills and abilities outlined under the Technical Qualifications and Executive Core Qualifications listed below. Typically, experience of this nature will have been gained at or above the equivalent of the GS-15 grade level in the Federal service or its equivalent with state and local government, the private sector, or non-governmental organizations. To meet the minimum qualification requirements for this position, you must show that you possess the five Executive Core Qualifications (ECQs) and the Technical Qualifications (TQs) listed below. We recommend that your resume emphasize your level of responsibilities, the scope and complexity of programs managed, and your program accomplishments, including results of your actions. The application process used to recruit for this position is RESUME-ONLY. YOUR RESUME MUST NOT EXCEED 2 PAGES. Any resumes over the 2-page limit, will not be reviewed beyond page 2 or may be disqualified. There is NO requirement to prepare a narrative statement specifically addressing the Executive Core Qualifications (ECQs) or the Technical Qualifications (TQs). TECHNICAL QUALIFICATIONS (TQs): Your resume should demonstrate accomplishments that would satisfy the technical qualifications. Candidates must possess experience at the senior level (GS-14/15 level or equivalent) in the job-specific Technical Qualifications (TQs). The TQs measure the technical expertise required by this position and must be addressed within your 2-page resume. It is recommended that corresponding TQs be annotated in parenthesis within your 2-page resume. TQ 1: Knowledge of and experience overseeing complex international trade or border security investigative and/or enforcement programs. EXECUTIVE CORE QUALIFICATIONS (ECQs): In addition to the Technical Qualification Requirements listed above, all new entrants into the Senior Executive Service (SES) under a career appointment will be assessed for executive competency against the following five mandatory ECQs. If your 2-page resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of the ECQs and TQs, you may not receive further consideration for the position. jobs.title: Director of Philanthropy
jobs.description:
About Just A Start

Founded in 1968 in Cambridge, Massachusetts, Just A Start is a community development corporation that builds homes, careers and futures .

Just A Start believes that access to stable housing and sustainable careers are the essential building blocks of equitable communities. For 58 years, we have focused on meeting the fundamental needs of individuals and families who have been systemically denied opportunities to realize their full potential. Our programs include affordable housing development and services, career training for adults and youth, and financial empowerment programs, spanning Cambridge, the Metro North region and Boston.

We have developed and operate 750 affordable apartments. To keep community members housed, we also offer financial and technical assistance to prevent evictions and support low- and moderate-income homeowners. Finally, we prepare individuals of all ages and circumstances with the skills and knowledge they need to secure fulfilling careers, leveraging their talents to achieve economic mobility and strengthen the region’s workforce.

Mission Statement:
Just A Start promotes equity by creating access to stable housing and building pathways to economic opportunity.

Vision Statement
: Just A Start’s vision is an equitable community where everyone can secure a solid economic foundation.

Our Impact

We have developed and own 750 affordable homes, housing approximately 1,800 people, with another 350 homes planned over the next 5-7 years.
Each year, we help 600+ people with rental assistance, housing stabilization, homelessness prevention, and home improvement services.
We train nearly 100 adults annually for careers in biomedical and IT fields and support 50 youth with career training in construction, entrepreneurship, and green jobs. Upon securing employment, graduates of our IT and biomedical programs see an average annual income increase of $20,000.
We provide 150 people annually with financial coaching and education to help them plan and save for their futures.
Our free tax preparation services return approximately $650,000 each year to low- and moderate-income community members.

Looking Ahead: Completed Capital Campaign, Economic Mobility Hub, and 5-Year Strategic Plan

Just A Start completed its first-ever capital campaign in 2022-2024 to support the development of our Economic Mobility Hub, a 70,000 square foot, 6-story building that houses Just A Start’s headquarters, and space for well-integrated services including career training for youths and adults, financial empowerment, 24 affordable apartments, housing resources, and pre-kindergarten classes.

We raised $5.6 million through the campaign, exceeding the campaign goal of $4.25 million by 30%. The campaign was successful in raising funds, expanding and engaging donors, and elevating the organization’s profile. Over 60% of gifts came from first-time donors. Riding on the success of the campaign, we have room to grow our individual and business donors.

With the opening of the Economic Mobility Hub in 2024, we embarked on a five-year strategic plan (2025-2029) that emphasizes not just what we do, but how we do it. Our “how” includes a commitment to diversity and inclusion, program integration, learning and evaluation, and a participant-centered approach. The plan focuses on enhancing, expanding and better integrating our work to support economic mobility through housing, careers, and financial empowerment. It also maps out our fund development plan, including promoting a culture of philanthropy across the organization, building partnerships, and amplifying our impacts.

The Opportunity

Just A Start is seeking a Director of Philanthropy

Just A Start is seeking a passionate, experienced, and dedicated Director of Philanthropy to lead our Philanthropy team to advance Just A Start’s mission by ensuring the organization’s long-term financial sustainability, and by raising Just A Start’s profile through strategic marketing and communication initiatives.

Reporting to the Executive Director and serving as a member of the Leadership Team, the Director of Philanthropy manages the Philanthropy team, which includes the Associate Director of Institutional Giving, Associate Director of Communications, and Philanthropy Associate. The Director of Philanthropy also staffs the Board of Directors’ Fundraising Committee. In this leadership capacity, the Director is a strategic thought partner for program directors and the Executive Director.

The incoming Director will build on Just A Start’s strong fundraising foundation and successful capital campaign to shape the next phase of the organization’s philanthropy program. Key priorities will include strengthening and diversifying the donor pipeline, developing the next iteration of the major gifts program, deepening Board and donor engagement, and building on the strong foundation already established to further advance Just A Start’s fundraising strategies, systems, and future goals .

Key Responsibilities

The Director of Philanthropy will be charged with providing strategic leadership, planning, implementation, and partnership on all aspects of fund development and communications.

In 2026, Just A Start’s annual budget is $10.5 million, supported by a diverse mix of government, philanthropic, earned, and real estate-related revenue. The Philanthropy Team is currently responsible for raising approximately $3 million annually. This fundraising goal is expected to evolve and likely increase over the next several years as Just A Start grows its programs and navigates a changing funding landscape.

Key Job Activities

Philanthropy

Develop and execute a comprehensive annual and multi-year fundraising strategy aligned with organizational priorities and future strategic planning efforts.
Work in partnership with the Executive Director, the Board of Directors, the Leadership Team, and Just A Start staff on all major fundraising initiatives.
Develop and implement an annual fund development plan, and special fund initiatives such as endowment and planned gifts. Create strategies to raise funds from diverse funding sources, including foundations, corporations, government, and individuals - direct mail and major gifts.
Lead and evolve Just A Start’s major gifts program, managing the full donor cycle from identification and cultivation through solicitation and stewardship. The Director will help shape the next iteration of the program, including refining major gift strategies, donor segmentation, and giving levels to align with Just A Start's evolving goals.
Oversee fundraising systems, operations, and infrastructure to ensure accurate donor data, effective prospect tracking, timely reporting, and efficient fundraising processes, including management and optimization of Salesforce CRM.
Lead, manage, and develop the Philanthropy Team, setting clear priorities and performance goals, fostering collaboration and accountability, and ensuring successful execution of annual fundraising goals and longer-term strategic initiatives.

Executive Leadership and Board Engagement

As a member of the Leadership Team, actively participate in organizational strategy, management, budgeting, culture-building, and internal communication. Provide leadership in advancing, implementing, and monitoring Just A Start’s strategic plan.
Serve as a strategic thought partner to the Executive Director and Leadership Team, bringing a philanthropy, communications, and external-relations perspective to organizational decision-making.
Help foster a strong culture of philanthropy across the organization, engaging leaders and staff in understanding their roles in building relationships, communicating impact, and advancing Just A Start’s mission.
Serve as the primary staff liaison to the Board Fundraising Committee, partnering with committee leadership to establish priorities, develop strategies, and track progress toward fundraising goals.
Engage and support the full Board of Directors in giving, fundraising, donor cultivation, and stewardship, and help Board members serve effectively as ambassadors for Just A Start.
Provide Board members with the information, tools, messaging, and opportunities they need to confidently represent the organization and strengthen relationships with donors, partners, and other key stakeholders.

Marketing & Communications

Provide strategic oversight of Marketing and Communications, partnering with the Associate Director of Communications to strengthen Just A Start's visibility, messaging, brand positioning, and donor engagement.
Oversee the implementation of a comprehensive marketing/communications plan annually for Just A Start that continues to increase and strengthen the visibility and awareness of the organization.

External Relations

Cultivate and maintain a strong network of new community, corporate, philanthropic, government, and civic relationships that expands Just A Start’s visibility, strengthens its reputation, and creates new opportunities for partnership and support.
Steward and deepen existing partnerships by leading the partner relationship management in collaboration with the Executive Director, program directors and other colleagues.
Represent the organization and be an effective ambassador at outside events and activities.
Strengthen Just A Start’s external presence and reputation by identifying opportunities for organizational visibility, thought leadership, speaking engagements, community participation, and other forums that advance the organization’s mission and strategic priorities.

Candidate Profile

The Ideal Candidate Will Be a Strategic, Mission-driven Philanthropy Leader Who Is Energized By The Opportunity To Build Upon Just A Start’s Strong Foundation And Expand Our Community Of Supporters And Partners. They Will Bring The Following Capabilities

Strategic, Visionary, and Entrepreneurial Leader: A forward-thinking leader who can translate Just A Start’s mission and strategic priorities into a compelling, comprehensive philanthropy strategy. The successful candidate will balance long-term vision with strong execution, establishing clear goals, using data to assess progress, bringing initiative, curiosity, and adaptability to identifying and building new opportunities to strengthen Just A Start’s visibility and financial sustainability.
Relationship Builder and Ambassador: A skilled relationship builder with the confidence, presence, and credibility to represent Just A Start externally and inspire engagement among individual donors, corporations, foundations, government partners, board members, and community stakeholders. They will communicate the organization’s impact in a compelling and accessible way, and cultivate relationships that expand our reach and support.
Collaborative Strategic Partner: A trusted and collaborative partner who will work closely with the Executive Director, Board of Directors, Leadership Team, program leaders, and staff across the organization. They will promote a culture of philanthropy, strengthen coordination across departments, and help colleagues understand their role in advancing Just A Start’s external presence.
Experienced Fundraising and Communications Leader: A results-oriented professional with a demonstrated record of developing and implementing successful fundraising strategies across multiple revenue streams. They will understand how philanthropy, marketing, communications, and external relations reinforce one another and will provide effective leadership and support to a talented team responsible for these functions.
Supportive and Accountable People Manager: An inclusive and effective manager who sets clear priorities, supports professional growth, encourages collaboration, and holds themselves and others accountable for results. They will bring sound judgment, adaptability, and a willingness to remain engaged in both strategic leadership and hands-on execution.

Development and Outreach Department

The Role

The Chief Development Officer (CDO) will bring fresh vision and strategic leadership to build on and boldly advance the organization's fundraising, marketing, and donor and community engagement efforts, deepening impact and expanding reach at a pivotal moment for HRW. This is a critical position for the organization and an exciting opportunity to shape and accelerate the fundraising strategy and roadmap for HRW's future, developing and implementing ambitious fundraising, outreach, and constituency building strategies. The CDO must be committed to HRW's mission to take on human rights abuses around the world, communicate passionately about its work, and inspire its staff, volunteer teams, and donors.

The CDO will report directly to Executive Director Philippe Bolopion and will serve on HRW's Executive Committee, the organization’s senior leadership team. The CDO will lead a high-performing Development & Outreach Team of approximately 110 staff members, spanning leadership and principal giving, donor committees and council fundraising, Board of Directors engagement, foundation giving, marketing, planned giving, and fundraising systems and data analysis.

Fundraising Context

HRW’s fundraising has grown steadily over the years, and it currently raises approximately $100M annually, with approximately 70% of its revenue from gifts of $100,000+. A focus of fundraising and outreach at HRW has been the HRW Council, a collective of some 20 committees and 1,000 individuals around the world who help fundraise, engage new constituents and potential donors, partner with local organizations to promote human rights issues, and advocate on behalf of HRW and its mission. The CDO will be responsible for growing existing revenue streams and diversifying the organization’s income through principal, leadership and major gifts, institutional funding, marketing, and planned giving to ensure the long-term health and sustainability of the organization.

The greatest opportunity for the CDO lies in engaging donors at the highest levels to support major strategic work while also determining the optimal level of resources for growing the base of support. In 2024, HRW adopted a five-year Global Strategy to guide the organization’s programmatic and operational direction. In July 2026, the strategy was refined to help position HRW for maximum impact in a rapidly shifting human rights environment. The CDO will shape how HRW grows and diversifies revenue to support the organization’s strategic priorities and deliver on the ambitions set out in the refined strategy.

Underpinning all of this is a mandate for stability and steady leadership. HRW seeks a CDO who will lead the function credibly over the long term – reinforcing continuity, strengthening the pipeline, and building the confidence of the Development & Outreach Team. The CDO will partner closely with an engaged Board, providing the structure and clear, well-framed strategies that enable board members to fundraise effectively, and bringing the judgment and gravitas to offer candid counsel to both the Board and the Executive Director. The Executive Director is a highly effective, door-opening presence with donors, and the CDO will amplify that strength through strategic partnership, disciplined preparation, and timely briefings. Finally, the CDO will invest in the Development & Outreach Team itself – building capacity, fostering trust across a distributed group, and marrying HRW's activist passion with professional fundraising rigor.

Key Responsibilities

Play a critical leadership role in shaping the organization's overall strategy and multi-year financial planning, working closely with the Executive Committee and Finance team to align revenue growth with organizational priorities;
Translate those priorities into an ambitious multi-year development and fundraising strategy, developing and implementing compelling plans and campaigns that inspire donors and partners to join HRW in addressing unprecedented challenges to human rights;
Provide strategic direction across all aspects of HRW fundraising and outreach activities, including leadership gifts, foundations, marketing, donor experiences, planned giving, development operations and analysis, donor committees and board engagement;
Represent HRW’s work to donors, prospects, and the Council to cultivate and grow the organization’s base of support;
Set and meet fundraising objectives, monitor and evaluate progress, and pivot strategy as needed to capitalize on emerging opportunities and maximize impact;
Develop comprehensive, ambitious funding proposals that will engage and inspire top-tier donors to make transformational gifts;
Champion diversity, equity, and inclusion within the Development & Outreach Team and across relationships with donors, board, and committee members;
Determine the appropriate short and long-term investments in development, setting budgets, leveraging data analytics, and maximizing revenue while building a robust pipeline of major and planned giving donors;
Collaborate across the organization to ensure development activities are well coordinated with and supportive of organizational priorities;
Support and amplify fundraising efforts of the Executive Director, senior leadership, and Development & Outreach Team;
Sustain and strengthen Board of Directors engagement and stewardship in consultation with organizational leadership;
Lead, motivate and mentor a high performing team, setting clear expectations, establishing performance objectives, providing timely and constructive feedback, supporting professional growth, and attending to staff well- being and resilience;
Foster an inclusive, positive work environment where all staff feel welcome, heard and able to succeed, actively soliciting diverse perspectives, advancing equity and inclusion, and addressing any bias or discrimination proactively; and
Perform other tasks as may be required.

Candidate Profile

The Chief Development Officer will be a collaborative, innovative, and visionary leader with exceptional people, communications, and management skills and the passion and capacity to lead a sophisticated global fundraising operation. They will bring high intellectual and emotional intelligence, sharp cultural awareness, and the ability to communicate and influence effectively across a complex, highly distributed organization. The ideal candidate will understand the nuances of fundraising across multiple geographies and cultures, inspire and motivate experienced teams, and embody a deep commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion. They will be passionate about HRW's mission and able to articulate a compelling vision that engages staff, volunteers, advocates, and donors, and catalyzes giving.

Ideal Experience

At least 12 to 15 years of fundraising experience, with at least five (5) years of experience in a senior role such as Chief Development Officer, Deputy Chief Development Officer, or equivalent.
A deep commitment to HRW's mission of defending the rights of people worldwide, and the ability to communicate about its work with passion and conviction.
Proven experience leading and motivating fundraising teams in a complex, global organization, setting ambitious objectives, managing performance, and driving results.

The Managing Director, Data, AI & Applied Technology advances The Nature Conservancy (TNC)'s conservation mission by defining how data, applied technology, and artificial intelligence create measurable mission and business value. This is a newly created role and a first-of-its-kind function at TNC: it owns the “what, who, and why” of data, applied technology, and AI, including what decisions must improve, what outcomes matter most, where data can create mission advantage, and how emerging technologies should be responsibly explored and applied. The role then translates these insights into coordinated, collaborative execution to deliver measurable outcomes.

This role leads enterprise business data strategy, domain data ownership, data governance accountability, responsible AI governance, use-case prioritization, value realization, and adoption, and partners closely with the CIO organization, which owns technical data platforms, architecture, engineering, controls, and scalable delivery.

Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer with a dotted line to the Chief Executive Officer, and a dotted-line partnership with the Chief Information Officer, the Managing Director serves as TNC's senior authority on business data and AI strategy and governance, applied and emerging conservation technology, the NatureChat and conservation intelligence workstreams, technology partnerships, and external thought leadership and cross-NGO positioning.

In This Role, You Will

Develop and maintain TNC's enterprise business data, applied technology, and AI strategies, aligned to conservation priorities and organizational goals.
Establish and mature a federated domain data ownership model across Conservation, Science, Development/Membership, Marketing, HR, Finance, Legal, Operations, and other enterprise domains.
Lead enterprise data governance from a business accountability perspective, and establish responsible AI governance guidance, acceptable-use expectations, and risk-review processes.
Build executive and domain-leader commitment to data stewardship, data quality, responsible AI, and adoption, and develop data and AI literacy programs in partnership with People, Learning, IT, and business domains.
Build and manage a high-performing, globally aware team spanning business data strategy and governance, responsible AI, portfolio management, adoption, and data culture.
Operate as an enterprise partner and trusted advisor to the Executive Leadership Team, and represent TNC in external forums on responsible AI, conservation data, and mission-driven data strategy.
Manage an annual operating budget covering team, tools, and external services, and negotiate and manage contracts with vendors and service partners.

You will navigate the unique dynamics of a globally federated organization, building consensus across regions and business units while maintaining enterprise standards, and champion a culture where people at every level can confidently use data to make decisions.

We’re Looking For You

Are you energized by the chance to build something that has never existed at TNC before? This is a rare opportunity to shape a brand-new enterprise function from the ground up, one that will define how data, applied technology, and artificial intelligence help protect the lands and waters all life depends on.

You will work at the center of TNC's federated, global structure, partnering with the Chief Operating Officer, Chief Executive Officer, Chief Information Officer, and Executive Leadership Team to translate emerging technology into real conservation and business outcomes. You will help TNC evolve into an organization where timely, trusted data informs decisions at every level, from field-based conservation teams to the executive suite.

If you thrive on ambiguity, enjoy building consensus across a complex global organization, and want your work on data and AI to translate directly into mission impact, we would love to hear from you. This position is hybrid, with a preference for candidates based in the Washington, DC metro area near TNC's Arlington, VA office, though flexibility exists for candidates located elsewhere.

Bachelor's degree in business, law, data science, data governance, natural resource management, or other relevant field and 10 or more years of experience, including 5 years of experience at a senior level in a global and/or multi-product line organization, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
Experience in partnership development with corporations, community leaders, governments, and non-profit organizations in multiple countries, including experience with high-level government and conservation contacts.
Experience translating organizational strategy into data, analytics, applied technology, or AI-enabled business outcomes.
Experience with executive-level communication and influence, including building credibility with non-technical senior audiences and technical partners.
Experience leading governance, decision rights, adoption strategies, change management, and benefits realization across a matrixed organization.
Experience with data privacy, security, ethical data use, responsible AI, and inclusive change leadership.

Graduate degree in business, law, data science, data governance, natural resource management, and/or other relevant field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
Experience in global, federated, or mission-driven organizations.
Experience establishing federated data governance, responsible AI governance, domain data ownership, or data product operating models.
Familiarity with conservation science data, geospatial data, fundraising or donor data, marketing data, HR or people data, finance data, or comparable complex data domains.
Track record building organizational data literacy and adoption, encompassing culture and behavior change, not just tools.
Experience cultivating external technology partnerships, academic collaborations, in-kind support, or pro bono expertise.
Comfort with ambiguity and an entrepreneurial approach, including experience shaping a new enterprise function while maintaining governance discipline.

The Nature Conservancy’s mission is to protect the lands and waters upon which all life depends. About Just A Start

Founded in 1968 in Cambridge, Massachusetts, Just A Start is a community development corporation that builds homes, careers and futures .

Just A Start believes that access to stable housing and sustainable careers are the essential building blocks of equitable communities. For 58 years, we have focused on meeting the fundamental needs of individuals and families who have been systemically denied opportunities to realize their full potential. Our programs include affordable housing development and services, career training for adults and youth, and financial empowerment programs, spanning Cambridge, the Metro North region and Boston.

We have developed and operate 750 affordable apartments. To keep community members housed, we also offer financial and technical assistance to prevent evictions and support low- and moderate-income homeowners. Finally, we prepare individuals of all ages and circumstances with the skills and knowledge they need to secure fulfilling careers, leveraging their talents to achieve economic mobility and strengthen the region’s workforce.

Mission Statement:
Just A Start promotes equity by creating access to stable housing and building pathways to economic opportunity.

Vision Statement
: Just A Start’s vision is an equitable community where everyone can secure a solid economic foundation.

Our Impact

We have developed and own 750 affordable homes, housing approximately 1,800 people, with another 350 homes planned over the next 5-7 years.
Each year, we help 600+ people with rental assistance, housing stabilization, homelessness prevention, and home improvement services.
We train nearly 100 adults annually for careers in biomedical and IT fields and support 50 youth with career training in construction, entrepreneurship, and green jobs. Upon securing employment, graduates of our IT and biomedical programs see an average annual income increase of $20,000.
We provide 150 people annually with financial coaching and education to help them plan and save for their futures.
Our free tax preparation services return approximately $650,000 each year to low- and moderate-income community members.

Looking Ahead: Completed Capital Campaign, Economic Mobility Hub, and 5-Year Strategic Plan

Just A Start completed its first-ever capital campaign in 2022-2024 to support the development of our Economic Mobility Hub, a 70,000 square foot, 6-story building that houses Just A Start’s headquarters, and space for well-integrated services including career training for youths and adults, financial empowerment, 24 affordable apartments, housing resources, and pre-kindergarten classes.

We raised $5.6 million through the campaign, exceeding the campaign goal of $4.25 million by 30%. The campaign was successful in raising funds, expanding and engaging donors, and elevating the organization’s profile. Over 60% of gifts came from first-time donors. Riding on the success of the campaign, we have room to grow our individual and business donors.

With the opening of the Economic Mobility Hub in 2024, we embarked on a five-year strategic plan (2025-2029) that emphasizes not just what we do, but how we do it. Our “how” includes a commitment to diversity and inclusion, program integration, learning and evaluation, and a participant-centered approach. The plan focuses on enhancing, expanding and better integrating our work to support economic mobility through housing, careers, and financial empowerment. It also maps out our fund development plan, including promoting a culture of philanthropy across the organization, building partnerships, and amplifying our impacts.

The Opportunity

Just A Start is seeking a Director of Philanthropy

Just A Start is seeking a passionate, experienced, and dedicated Director of Philanthropy to lead our Philanthropy team to advance Just A Start’s mission by ensuring the organization’s long-term financial sustainability, and by raising Just A Start’s profile through strategic marketing and communication initiatives.

Reporting to the Executive Director and serving as a member of the Leadership Team, the Director of Philanthropy manages the Philanthropy team, which includes the Associate Director of Institutional Giving, Associate Director of Communications, and Philanthropy Associate. The Director of Philanthropy also staffs the Board of Directors’ Fundraising Committee. In this leadership capacity, the Director is a strategic thought partner for program directors and the Executive Director.

The incoming Director will build on Just A Start’s strong fundraising foundation and successful capital campaign to shape the next phase of the organization’s philanthropy program. Key priorities will include strengthening and diversifying the donor pipeline, developing the next iteration of the major gifts program, deepening Board and donor engagement, and building on the strong foundation already established to further advance Just A Start’s fundraising strategies, systems, and future goals .

Key Responsibilities

The Director of Philanthropy will be charged with providing strategic leadership, planning, implementation, and partnership on all aspects of fund development and communications.

In 2026, Just A Start’s annual budget is $10.5 million, supported by a diverse mix of government, philanthropic, earned, and real estate-related revenue. The Philanthropy Team is currently responsible for raising approximately $3 million annually. This fundraising goal is expected to evolve and likely increase over the next several years as Just A Start grows its programs and navigates a changing funding landscape.

Key Job Activities

Philanthropy

Develop and execute a comprehensive annual and multi-year fundraising strategy aligned with organizational priorities and future strategic planning efforts.
Work in partnership with the Executive Director, the Board of Directors, the Leadership Team, and Just A Start staff on all major fundraising initiatives.
Develop and implement an annual fund development plan, and special fund initiatives such as endowment and planned gifts. Create strategies to raise funds from diverse funding sources, including foundations, corporations, government, and individuals - direct mail and major gifts.
Lead and evolve Just A Start’s major gifts program, managing the full donor cycle from identification and cultivation through solicitation and stewardship. The Director will help shape the next iteration of the program, including refining major gift strategies, donor segmentation, and giving levels to align with Just A Start's evolving goals.
Oversee fundraising systems, operations, and infrastructure to ensure accurate donor data, effective prospect tracking, timely reporting, and efficient fundraising processes, including management and optimization of Salesforce CRM.
Lead, manage, and develop the Philanthropy Team, setting clear priorities and performance goals, fostering collaboration and accountability, and ensuring successful execution of annual fundraising goals and longer-term strategic initiatives.

Executive Leadership and Board Engagement

As a member of the Leadership Team, actively participate in organizational strategy, management, budgeting, culture-building, and internal communication. Provide leadership in advancing, implementing, and monitoring Just A Start’s strategic plan.
Serve as a strategic thought partner to the Executive Director and Leadership Team, bringing a philanthropy, communications, and external-relations perspective to organizational decision-making.
Help foster a strong culture of philanthropy across the organization, engaging leaders and staff in understanding their roles in building relationships, communicating impact, and advancing Just A Start’s mission.
Serve as the primary staff liaison to the Board Fundraising Committee, partnering with committee leadership to establish priorities, develop strategies, and track progress toward fundraising goals.
Engage and support the full Board of Directors in giving, fundraising, donor cultivation, and stewardship, and help Board members serve effectively as ambassadors for Just A Start.
Provide Board members with the information, tools, messaging, and opportunities they need to confidently represent the organization and strengthen relationships with donors, partners, and other key stakeholders.

Marketing & Communications

Provide strategic oversight of Marketing and Communications, partnering with the Associate Director of Communications to strengthen Just A Start's visibility, messaging, brand positioning, and donor engagement.
Oversee the implementation of a comprehensive marketing/communications plan annually for Just A Start that continues to increase and strengthen the visibility and awareness of the organization.

External Relations

Cultivate and maintain a strong network of new community, corporate, philanthropic, government, and civic relationships that expands Just A Start’s visibility, strengthens its reputation, and creates new opportunities for partnership and support.
Steward and deepen existing partnerships by leading the partner relationship management in collaboration with the Executive Director, program directors and other colleagues.
Represent the organization and be an effective ambassador at outside events and activities.
Strengthen Just A Start’s external presence and reputation by identifying opportunities for organizational visibility, thought leadership, speaking engagements, community participation, and other forums that advance the organization’s mission and strategic priorities.

Candidate Profile

The Ideal Candidate Will Be a Strategic, Mission-driven Philanthropy Leader Who Is Energized By The Opportunity To Build Upon Just A Start’s Strong Foundation And Expand Our Community Of Supporters And Partners. They Will Bring The Following Capabilities

Strategic, Visionary, and Entrepreneurial Leader: A forward-thinking leader who can translate Just A Start’s mission and strategic priorities into a compelling, comprehensive philanthropy strategy. The successful candidate will balance long-term vision with strong execution, establishing clear goals, using data to assess progress, bringing initiative, curiosity, and adaptability to identifying and building new opportunities to strengthen Just A Start’s visibility and financial sustainability.
Relationship Builder and Ambassador: A skilled relationship builder with the confidence, presence, and credibility to represent Just A Start externally and inspire engagement among individual donors, corporations, foundations, government partners, board members, and community stakeholders. They will communicate the organization’s impact in a compelling and accessible way, and cultivate relationships that expand our reach and support.
Collaborative Strategic Partner: A trusted and collaborative partner who will work closely with the Executive Director, Board of Directors, Leadership Team, program leaders, and staff across the organization. They will promote a culture of philanthropy, strengthen coordination across departments, and help colleagues understand their role in advancing Just A Start’s external presence.
Experienced Fundraising and Communications Leader: A results-oriented professional with a demonstrated record of developing and implementing successful fundraising strategies across multiple revenue streams. They will understand how philanthropy, marketing, communications, and external relations reinforce one another and will provide effective leadership and support to a talented team responsible for these functions.
Supportive and Accountable People Manager: An inclusive and effective manager who sets clear priorities, supports professional growth, encourages collaboration, and holds themselves and others accountable for results. They will bring sound judgment, adaptability, and a willingness to remain engaged in both strategic leadership and hands-on execution.
